title: Shot Down: The True Story of Pilot Howard Snyder and the Crew of the B-17 Susan Ruth
author: Steve Snyder
target_audience: Those interested in true stories of survival
core_themes: The impact of war on individuals and families
Allies and resistance in occupied Europe
Survival, escape, and evasion behind enemy lines
primary_purpose: To recount in vivid detail the experiences of Howard Snyder and his B-17 crew after their plane was shot down over Europe in 1944, exploring their struggle for survival with the help of the Belgian resistance, and illuminating the broader realities faced by American airmen in World War II.

structure_format.narrative_style: Third-person, historical narrative combined with first-hand accounts
structure_format.organization: Chronological, following the crew from initial training, through missions over Europe, to the period after being shot down and eventual liberation
features: Interweaves official documents, letters, and diary entries
Contains first-hand testimonies from survivors and locals
Includes photographs, maps, and archival images

key_concepts_lessons: The dangers and heroism inherent in daylight bombing missions over Europe.
The personal experiences of American airmen and their families.
The crucial role played by the European resistance in aiding downed Allied airmen.
Humanity in the midst of war—built on bonds of trust, compassion, and sacrifice.
The lingering effects of war trauma and loss on veterans and their loved ones.
notable_features: Focus on a specific crew and their individual fates
Personal connection—written by the pilot’s son
Provides both immediate narrative and contextual wartime history
cultural_historical_context: Reflects ongoing interest in World War II history and the sacrifices of the 'Greatest Generation.' Highlights the role of the Belgian resistance and the peril faced by downed Allied crews in Nazi-occupied Europe. Draws on declassified material and first-person accounts to document a microcosm of the wider air war.
reception_impact: Widely praised for its research depth and engaging, personal storytelling
Honored with several book awards, especially in military and nonfiction categories
Used as a reference in educational and veterans’ programs
Offered new perspectives for families of World War II servicemen
comparable_titles: Unbroken: A World War II Story of Survival, Resilience, and Redemption by Laura Hillenbrand
